items.title: Finding Zero-Days in Plain Sight: Our Security Team’s Uptoskills Penetration Testing Journey
items.one_liner: This writeup demonstrates how manual testing and direct origin discovery can bypass WAFs to uncover critical vulnerabilities that automated scanners miss.
items.summary: A penetration testing team identified critical security flaws in the Uptoskills platform by bypassing Cloudflare WAF protections through direct origin IP access. The team discovered vulnerabilities including CORS misconfigurations, subdomain takeovers, unauthenticated PII leakage, and exposed GitHub repositories containing credentials. These findings highlight the limitations of automated scanners, which were blocked by edge defenses, compared to manual business logic analysis.
key_facts: Bypass method: Direct origin IP access
Findings: CORS, PII leakage, credential exposure
items.bottom_line: Relying solely on automated scanners is insufficient, as WAFs can be bypassed by identifying and targeting the origin server directly.

claims.text: The team identified critical security flaws in the Uptoskills platform by bypassing Cloudflare WAF protections through direct origin IP access.
claims.support_span: By modifying HTTP host headers and sending requests directly to these IP addresses rather than the primary domain (uptoskills.com), we successfully bypassed all Cloudflare WAF rules.

claims.text: The team discovered vulnerabilities including CORS misconfigurations, subdomain takeovers, unauthenticated PII leakage, and exposed GitHub repositories containing credentials.

items.one_liner: Cisco released an IOS XR software hardening release to address internally discovered exceptional handling vulnerabilities grouped under CVE-2026-20280.

items.title: How one hedge-fund manager built his firm to be powered entirely by AI agents
items.one_liner: A hedge fund has successfully replaced its human staff with AI agents, demonstrating a massive reduction in operational costs.
items.summary: Hedge-fund manager Brian Kelly has transitioned his firm, Bracket22, to be powered entirely by AI agents, reducing annual labor-related costs from approximately $5 million to between $30,000 and $40,000. The firm uses specialized agents for technical analysis, quantitative strategies, and mission control, with Kelly providing final human oversight. Kelly suggests the primary opportunity for firms is not just replacement, but increasing the productivity of existing human staff by tenfold.
items.bottom_line: The successful deployment of AI agents in high-stakes trading environments signals a shift toward agentic workflows that can drastically lower operational overhead while maintaining productivity.
